moments.selftext: 🇨🇳 China's satellites are starting to sound a LOT like Skynet They successfully launched a sea-based Smart Dragon-3 rocket, carrying two AI-powered satellites into orbit. This isn't just another satellite launch. Sea-based launches make China's space program more flexible, harder to predict, and less dependent on a handful of fixed launch sites. More importantly, the satellites can reportedly process intelligence in orbit instead of waiting for instructions from the ground. In other words, Beijing isn't just building more satellites; it's building satellites that can think for themselves. What could possibly go wrong?!?! Source: @PressTV / Writers: Samuel, Ian

moments.title: The UK’s @AISecurityInst (AISI) has published a report on their recent cybersecurity evaluation of Anthropic’s Claude Mythos 5 and OpenAI’s GPT-5.6 Sol. The models attempted to complete an assignment in a setup where the
moments.selftext: The UK’s @AISecurityInst (AISI) has published a report on their recent cybersecurity evaluation of Anthropic’s Claude Mythos 5 and OpenAI’s GPT-5.6 Sol. The models attempted to complete an assignment in a setup where their normal safeguards were removed and they were deliberately given internet access. AISI reports that the models “engaged in sustained, potentially harmful activity directed at real people and organisations”. We’re grateful to AISI for their leadership in the important discussion about how to evaluate increasingly capable AI agents. We’re working closely with them to gather more details of the incident as we conduct our own investigation. Gaining a clear picture of Claude’s understanding of its situation—by examining its reasoning transcripts and running our own analyses—will help us identify the causes of its behavior. The prompts in the evaluation did not impose any specific restrictions on how the internet should be used. This and the removal of safeguards meant that the models were tested under “deliberately permissive conditions” that are not representative of any of our production models. Note that there was no evidence here of an escape from a secure environment. AISI’s disclosure of the incident can be found here:

moments.title: 🇩🇪 1,051 German lawyers just signed a letter to ban a party millions of Germans keep voting for. Judges, prosecutors and legal experts all say the AfD is unconstitutional and want the courts to shut it down before it cli
moments.selftext: 🇩🇪 1,051 German lawyers just signed a letter to ban a party millions of Germans keep voting for. Judges, prosecutors and legal experts all say the AfD is unconstitutional and want the courts to shut it down before it climbs any higher in the polls. The timing gives it away. The AfD is now one of the strongest parties in the country, so the move is to remove it by ruling instead of by vote. And here's the catch. Under German law, regular citizens get no say in this. Only the government, the Bundestag or the Bundesrat can ask the Constitutional Court to kill off a party. So a leading opposition party could be banned by the exact establishment it's beating. Whatever you think of the AfD, that part should worry everyone. Source: Spiegel. de / Writer: Daniyal

moments.selftext: Sayoko Yamaguchi, widely regarded as one of the most influential models to emerge from the 1970s fashion scene. Sayoko Yamaguchi was a revolutionary force in fashion and arguably the most influential Asian model of the 1970s. With her distinctive doll-like features, sharp bob haircut, and dramatic eyeliner, she challenged conventional beauty ideals and helped redefine the global fashion landscape by bringing Japanese aesthetics to the forefront. After making her Paris runway debut in 1972, Yamaguchi quickly became a favorite of visionary designers including Issey Miyake, Kenzo Takada, and Kansai Yamamoto. In 1973, she signed an exclusive worldwide contract with cosmetics powerhouse Shiseido, becoming the face of a campaign that showcased Japanese beauty and design to international audiences while reshaping perceptions within the fashion industry. Her international impact was further recognized in 1977, when Newsweek named her among the world’s six leading fashion models. That same year, her unforgettable image appeared on the cover of Steely Dan’s acclaimed album Aja. Rejecting the idea of being merely a model, Yamaguchi described herself as a “wearist,” viewing fashion as a form of expression and performance. Her influence was so enduring that mannequin designer Adel Rootstein created highly sought-after life-sized mannequins modeled after her iconic appearance, preserving her image as a symbol of fashion history.
